title: Haley Hopkins’ late goal earns Kansas City an NWSL Championship spot, revenge over Gotham FC
content:
The Kansas City Current are heading to the NWSL Championship to face the Washington Spirit after defeating reigning champions and NWSL Shield winners Gotham FC 2-1 on Sunday on Randall’s Island.

Current midfielder Croix Bethune provided a spark in the first half with her free-kick goal, and despite an own goal putting Gotham back into the game at home at Icahn Stadium, Current forward Haley Hopkins struck in the 89th minute with a winning goal off the crossbar to end Gotham’s hope of a repeat.

The Current got revenge against Gotham, which entered last year’s playoffs as the eighth and final seed, then upset Kansas City at home in the quarterfinals after KC’s historic regular season.

There were massive changes for the Current between that result and this one, particularly in the technical staff.

The Current hired Chris Armas as their new head coach in January, despite the former U.S. men’s national team midfielder’s lack of NWSL experience, after Vlatko Andonovski shifted into a new role as the club’s global sporting director (a new position which did not last the season). Additionally, the Current were without the services of star forward and two-time MVP Temwa Chawinga in last year’s quarterfinal due to injury.

While Gotham FC controlled possession, the Current were able to control every other element of Sunday’s match. The Athletic breaks down how it happened.

Hopkins scored one goal last season. The Current forward has 13 this season, the most of anyone on the team. It’s a seismic improvement made even sweeter by the fact that she capped off her tally with the most important one yet.

The momentum of the match had been heading in one of two ways: toward extra time or with a Gotham shock-victory.

Despite having zero shots on target all game, the reigning champions were buoyed by the own goal that brought them level with the Current, but a handball by Gotham fullback Guro Reiten in the 88th minute offered KC some reprieve. Fullback Izzy Rodriguez provided an exquisite ball toward the back post, a ball that Hopkins said in her ESPN postgame interview was the result of a last-second adjustment from Current assistant coach Lucas Rodriguez, who handles set pieces.

She was instructed to pull away toward the back side of the goal and struck her left-footed volley perfectly, sending it past Gotham goalkeeper Ann-Katrin Berger, clanging against the post before it bounced in.

That both the Current’s goals came from set pieces speaks to their clinical approach to the game for a team that is happy out of possession. It will come in handy in the final against the Spirit, and Hopkins is proving a key ingredient to their secret sauce. — Tamerra Griffin

The FAA ground stop delayed the Kansas City Current’s trip to New York for this semifinal, but it was scarcely apparent by kickoff at Icahn Stadium on Sunday afternoon. From kickoff, they were ravenous and direct, aggressive in the attack and forcing Gotham goalkeeper Ann-Katrin Berger to demonstrate why she earned another Goalkeeper of the Year nomination. Kansas City created more high-quality chances despite having far less of the ball — 33% to Gotham’s 67%, according to ESPN.

Midfielder Croix Bethune’s sublime free kick in the 20th minute wasn’t just an important manifestation of the Current’s front-footedness. It showed how capable she is of meeting the moment in a high-stakes game.

That had been clear in the sequence that led to the set piece. Current center back Gabby Robinson intercepted a ball at midfield and left it for Bethune, who dribbled toward goal at an angle that is difficult to defend without committing a foul. That is exactly what Gotham midfielder Denise O’Sullivan did, just outside the center of the penalty box. Bethune’s left-footed strike curled around Gotham midfielder Jaedyn Shaw, who was stationed at the outer edge of Gotham’s loosely assembled wall. Bethune, like Berger, is also in possession of an end-of-season award and might win her second as midfielder of the year. Moments like those — and the space she’s covered in this game — are why. — Griffin

Logic says you need shots on goal to win. For Gotham, that was not necessarily the case coming into Sunday’s semifinal. For the second playoff game in a row, they were able to produce an own goal to change the nature of the match. In the quarterfinal, the only goal was in the first five minutes off a Gotham corner kick, which proved the only tally needed against Seattle Reign.

In the semifinal, they had to wait. Despite withstanding the high press of the Current for most of the game, even as it contained their offensive play, Midge Purce made a promising run up the right wing in the 69th minute, booted the ball centrally, and defender Laney Rouse was the final one to push it over the goal line after a strange scramble from KC.

The own goal temporarily shifted the momentum of the match more towards Gotham, with Purce, Guro Reitan, Sam Kerr, Jaedyn Shaw and Rose Lavelle pushing forward with greater intent. None of those efforts resulted in a shot on goal, however.

And while Ann Katrin-Berger had put on a masterclass for much of the second half, particularly against Temwa Chawinga, that lack of offensive output finally betrayed Gotham with Hopkins’ late goal. —Meg Linehan

Arriving at Randalls Island on a ferry on one of the coldest sunny days of the year with hundreds of Gotham FC fans was an experience not to be forgotten. With tickets for the semifinal sold out within 10 minutes, Gotham fans wanted to make sure Icahn felt like home for the day.

Gotham fans were the majority in the long lines ahead of the match, but also at least 1,000 Kansas City Current fans arrived in New York from Kansas City, Hazleton, Pa., owner Chris Long’s hometown, and from Princeton University, where both Chris and Angie Long graduated.

Inside, Gotham supporters’ group Cloud Nine’s non-stop drums, cheers and energy continued throughout the 90 minutes even when the temperature dropped significantly after the sun set.

—Asli Pelit

The Kansas City Current will head to Washington, D.C., to face the Spirit in the NWSL Championship at 8 p.m. ET on Nov. 21. It will be the Current’s second shake at winning a championship trophy at Audi Field. They lost in 2022 to Sophia Wilson and the Portland Thorns.
